scope_note: A buyer's-guide survey of open-weight large language models a reader might run themselves, organized by what you'd actually use one for — general chat, roleplay/creative writing, reasoning, coding, multilingual, vision-capable, and small/edge-class models — rather than by architecture or lineage. This is not the roster OpenGauntlet benchmarks (see the leaderboard for that): it is a wider, editorial survey of the ecosystem, scoped to open-weight models only. No proprietary or cloud-only models (GPT, Claude, Gemini, etc.) appear here.
method_note: Every row is checked against a primary source — the model's own Hugging Face card, GitHub repo, or official release announcement — before publication, then adversarially audited in a second pass that actively tries to refute each field rather than confirm it, followed by a cross-category consolidation pass that deduplicates, rechecks every facet against the row's own (possibly-corrected) text, and drops anything that could not be verified rather than presenting a guess as fact.

systems.name: Llama 4 Scout (17B-16E-Instruct)
systems.best_for: Readers who want frontier-scale reasoning/knowledge with MoE efficiency and native multimodal (text+image) input, and are not blocked by Meta's 700M-MAU commercial cap.
systems.watch: The Llama 4 Community License requires a separate agreement from Meta for products/services with over 700M monthly active users in the preceding calendar month.
systems.standout: Native multimodal MoE with an unusually large stated context window (10M tokens) among open-weight releases. Notably, Llama 4 also DROPPED the anti-distillation clause present in the Llama 3 license, so unlike earlier Llama releases its outputs may legally be used to train other models.
systems.architecture: Mixture-of-experts (MoE) with early-fusion native multimodality (text+image input, text output); 16 experts, 17B active of 109B total parameters
systems.quantization_note: Community GGUF/INT4 quantizations exist; Meta states an INT4-quantized Scout is designed to fit a single H100 (80GB) GPU at reduced context. Weight footprint at 4-bit is an editorial estimate (~60GB), not a vendor-published minimum.
systems.verification_note: Confirmed against the official meta-llama/Llama-4-Scout-17B-16E-Instruct Hugging Face model card and the license text at developer.meta.com/ai/llama4/license/.

systems.name: Llama 3.1 8B Instruct
systems.best_for: A daily-driver chat model small enough to run comfortably on a single consumer GPU, for readers who want the Llama ecosystem (templates, tooling, community fine-tunes) without 70B-class VRAM cost.
systems.watch: Same Llama Community License catch as other Llama releases: a separate commercial licence is required above 700M monthly active users.
systems.standout: The most forked/fine-tuned small Llama base in the open ecosystem, with the broadest third-party tooling support of any 8B-class model.
systems.architecture: Dense auto-regressive transformer with grouped-query attention (GQA)
systems.quantization_note: Extremely wide GGUF quantization coverage (e.g. lmstudio-community); roughly 5-6GB at 4-bit, comfortably fits an 8GB card with context headroom.
systems.verification_note: Confirmed against the official meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct Hugging Face model card and its LICENSE file.

systems.name: Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507
systems.context_window: 262,144 tokens native (configurable further via long-context extension)
systems.best_for: Readers who want the strongest fully-permissive (Apache-2.0) open-weight chat model and can host a large MoE, for everyday conversation rather than explicit step-by-step reasoning.
systems.standout: Apache-2.0 licensed at genuine frontier scale, with no MAU cap or non-commercial catch, unlike the Llama and Gemma families at similar capability tiers. NOTE: the exact same Qwen3-235B-A22B base also ships as the separate Thinking-2507 checkpoint in this survey's reasoning category — a legitimately distinct, thinking-only fine-tune, not a duplicate listing.
systems.architecture: Mixture-of-experts, 94 layers, 128 experts with 8 activated per token, grouped-query attention (64 query / 4 KV heads); this is the non-thinking instruct variant and does not generate <think> blocks
systems.quantization_note: Even the 4-bit (Q4_K_M) GGUF is large: the official unsloth build is ~142GB across three shards (49.9+49.9+42.3GB), which exceeds a single 128GB unified-memory box, not just an 80GB card. Multi-GPU or unified-memory hardware well beyond one top-tier card is required at this quant level.
systems.verification_note: Confirmed against the official Qwen/Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507 Hugging Face model card; release window (July 21-22, 2025) and quantized file size independently corroborated via secondary sources.

systems.name: Qwen3-32B
systems.best_for: A single dense mid-size model for readers who want one weight set that handles fast everyday chat and, when needed, switches into a slower step-by-step reasoning mode.
systems.standout: One of the few open-weight models that toggles between fast chat and explicit chain-of-thought reasoning inside a single checkpoint, rather than shipping separate 'instruct' and 'thinking' releases.
systems.architecture: Dense transformer, 64 layers, grouped-query attention (64 query / 8 KV heads); switches between thinking mode (emits <think> blocks) and non-thinking mode within the same checkpoint
systems.quantization_note: GGUF and NVFP4 community quantizations available; roughly 18-20GB at 4-bit, fits a 24GB card with context headroom.
systems.verification_note: Confirmed against the official Qwen/Qwen3-32B Hugging Face model card; release date independently corroborated (matches exactly).

systems.name: Mistral Small 3.2 24B Instruct 2506
systems.best_for: A fully permissive, vision-capable 24B daily driver for readers who want strong instruction-following and reliable function-calling without any licence catch.
systems.standout: A minor point-release over 3.1 specifically targeting less repetition and a more reliable function-calling template — the kind of fix that matters more in daily use than a benchmark jump. NOTE: this same base lineage (Mistral-Small-3.2-24B-Instruct-2506) is also the base_model for three other rows in this survey — Cydonia 24B v4.3 (roleplay), Magistral-Small-2509 (reasoning), and Devstral-Small-2507 (coding) — each a genuinely distinct fine-tune for a different purpose, not a duplicate listing.
systems.architecture: Dense transformer with a vision encoder (text + image input, text output)
systems.quantization_note: GGUF community quantizations available (e.g. bartowski); roughly 13-14GB at 4-bit.
systems.verification_note: Confirmed against the official mistralai/Mistral-Small-3.2-24B-Instruct-2506 Hugging Face model card, including the WildBench/Arena Hard improvements over 3.1 and the reduced-repetition claim.

systems.name: Gemma 3 27B Instruct
systems.price_note: Free / self-host (gated download, Gemma Terms of Use)
systems.best_for: Readers who want Google's training/alignment recipe and multimodal (text+image) input in a size that fits a single high-end consumer GPU.
systems.watch: Access is gated behind acceptance of Google's Gemma Terms of Use and Prohibited Use Policy; Google retains the right to update the terms and restrict usage it deems non-compliant, and the licence's 'Model Derivatives' language reaches distillation, not just direct fine-tunes.
systems.architecture: Dense transformer, multimodal (images normalized to 896x896 resolution, encoded to 256 tokens each)
systems.quantization_note: GGUF community quantizations widely available (e.g. unsloth, lmstudio-community); roughly 15-16GB at 4-bit.
systems.verification_note: Confirmed against the official google/gemma-3-27b-it Hugging Face model card and the Gemma Terms of Use / Prohibited Use Policy; exact release date (March 12, 2025) independently corroborated via Google's own Gemma 3 announcement.

systems.name: DeepSeek-V3.2
systems.params: 671B total main model (685B including a 14B multi-token-prediction module), MoE
systems.best_for: Readers who want a fully MIT-licensed, frontier-scale open-weight chat model and have multi-GPU or unified-memory hardware to run it.
systems.standout: DeepSeek Sparse Attention is a genuine architectural change (not just a bigger training run) aimed specifically at long-context inference efficiency.
systems.architecture: Mixture-of-experts with DeepSeek Sparse Attention (DSA), a new attention mechanism aimed at long-context inference efficiency; builds on the V3.1-Terminus/V3.2-Exp lineage with an agentic task-synthesis training pipeline; supports both thinking and non-thinking modes with thinking integrated directly into tool-use
systems.quantization_note: Even at 4-bit the ~671B main model needs roughly 370GB of weight memory — multi-GPU or unified-memory hardware well beyond a single 128GB card. Community GGUF/FP8 builds exist (e.g. unsloth) for such setups.
systems.verification_note: License (MIT), DSA architecture, base_model repo name, and the December 1, 2025 release date are directly confirmed via the official deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2 Hugging Face card and DeepSeek's own API-docs announcement (api-docs.deepseek.com/news/news251201). However, repeated direct fetches of both the HF card and the linked GitHub README could NOT surface the 128K context window or 37B active-parameter figure anywhere in the card text for V3.2 specifically — those numbers follow the well-documented DeepSeek-V3 lineage and are corroborated only by independent secondary technical coverage, not restated verbatim on the V3.2 card itself.

systems.name: GLM-4.6
systems.best_for: Readers who want a fully permissive, frontier-scale open-weight chat model with one of the longer input context windows in this class.
systems.standout: Context window expanded from 128k to 200k over GLM-4.5 while keeping the same 357B/32B MoE shape.
systems.architecture: Mixture-of-experts (glm4_moe)
systems.quantization_note: Even at 4-bit the 357B model needs roughly 195GB of weight memory — beyond a single 128GB card. Official FP8 (zai-org) and community GGUF builds exist for multi-GPU deployment.
systems.verification_note: License (MIT), 357B total parameters, 200K context window, 128K max output, and glm4_moe architecture are directly confirmed on the official zai-org/GLM-4.6 Hugging Face card. The 32B active-parameter figure and the September 30, 2025 release date are NOT stated on the fetched card content itself and are corroborated only by independent secondary technical coverage. CONSOLIDATION PASS: dropped the 'reasoning-native' facet that appeared in the source row — none of this row's own text fields (best_for, standout, architecture, verification_note) describe a thinking/reasoning mode for this checkpoint, unlike the DeepSeek-V3.2 and Qwen3-32B rows which explicitly document one; the facet lacked textual support within this row.

systems.name: Command R+ (08-2024)
systems.price_note: Free for research/non-commercial use only; commercial use requires a separate licence from Cohere
systems.best_for: Researchers and hobbyists who want a strong RAG- and tool-use-tuned chat model for non-commercial local use; not a fit for anyone needing commercially-safe weights.
systems.watch: CC-BY-NC-4.0 is non-commercial only — despite being 'open weights', these cannot legally be used in a commercial product without a separate agreement from Cohere.
systems.standout: Purpose-built for RAG and multi-step tool use rather than general chit-chat, with citations as a first-class output format.
systems.architecture: Dense transformer with grouped-query attention (GQA), optimized for retrieval-augmented generation and multi-step tool use
systems.quantization_note: An official 4-bit build is published by Cohere Labs at CohereLabs/c4ai-command-r-plus-4bit (confirmed to exist); community GGUF quantizations also exist. Roughly 55-60GB at 4-bit.
systems.verification_note: Confirmed against the official CohereLabs/c4ai-command-r-plus-08-2024 Hugging Face model card; the official 4-bit repo (CohereLabs/c4ai-command-r-plus-4bit) independently confirmed to exist.

systems.name: Phi-4
systems.best_for: Readers who want a small, fully permissive dense model that punches above its weight on reasoning/STEM benchmarks and fits an ordinary 12-16GB GPU.
systems.standout: Trained with a heavy emphasis on synthetic data specifically to improve reasoning quality per parameter, rather than just scaling.
systems.architecture: Dense decoder-only transformer
systems.quantization_note: GGUF community quantizations widely available; roughly 8GB at 4-bit.
systems.verification_note: Confirmed against the official microsoft/phi-4 Hugging Face model card. Independently corroborated: Phi-4 was first published December 12, 2024 via Azure AI Foundry under a Microsoft Research License Agreement, then released on Hugging Face under MIT terms in January 2025. Also independently confirmed the base phi-4 model is English-only / not intended for multilingual use, unlike the separate phi-4-multimodal and phi-4-mini variants.

systems.name: Stheno v3.2 (L3-8B)
systems.price_note: Free to self-host; non-commercial licence only
systems.best_for: Balanced narrative roleplay and storywriting on modest 8GB-class hardware — one of the most widely used small-model RP fine-tunes, tuned for multi-turn character coherency and SFW/NSFW balance rather than raw explicitness.
systems.watch: CC-BY-NC-4.0 blocks commercial deployment; the author's own card says to message on Discord to arrange private/commercial hosting terms.
systems.standout: Explicitly trained to balance storywriting and roleplay data (Claude-3-Opus-style instruct data plus curated c2 roleplay logs) rather than optimizing for NSFW intensity alone.
systems.architecture: Llama 3 (dense, 8B)
systems.quantization_note: Widely re-quantized to GGUF by third parties (bartowski, QuantFactory, and others); also served by Featherless AI and Novita.
systems.fine_tuning: Full fine-tune of Llama 3 8B on Gryphe's Opus-WritingPrompts, Sao10K's Claude-3-Opus-Instruct-15K, Short-Storygen-v2, and filtered c2 roleplay logs.
systems.adoption: 336.7K downloads, 433 likes on Hugging Face (verified via HF API); among the most-downloaded community roleplay fine-tunes of its size.
systems.verification_note: License, base model, training datasets, download/like counts, and inference-provider listing (Novita, Featherless AI) all confirmed directly against the model's Hugging Face repo metadata via the HF Hub API. Exact context length is not explicitly restated in the card; 8k reflects the stock Llama 3 8B architecture it was trained on.

systems.name: Llama-3-Lumimaid 8B v0.1
systems.price_note: Free to self-host; non-commercial licence only
systems.context_window: 8k tokens (Llama 3 8B architecture; the README lists its LimaRP training component as run at 8k context)
systems.best_for: NSFW-forward, companion-style character roleplay in a compact 8B footprint from NeverSleep, one of the earliest teams to specialize purely in RP/ERP fine-tuning of Llama 3.
systems.watch: Card is self-tagged not-for-all-audiences/NSFW; CC-BY-NC-4.0 blocks commercial use.
systems.standout: One of the founding fine-tunes of the Llama-3 roleplay lineage, incorporating Undi95's earlier Llama-3-Unholy-8B-e4 and Llama-3-LewdPlay-8B into its 8B finetune process, that many later community RP merges trace back to.
systems.architecture: Llama 3 (dense, 8B)
systems.base_model: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B (exact instruct/base variant not stated in the card)
systems.quantization_note: GGUF builds available directly from NeverSleep; served on Featherless AI.
systems.fine_tuning: Fine-tune of Llama 3 8B built in part from Undi95's Llama-3-Unholy-8B-e4 and Llama-3-LewdPlay-8B, trained on Aesir, NoRobots, LimaRP, toxic-dpo-v0.1, ToxicQAFinal, Ikari's Luminae dataset, and PIPPA, with the card itself stating roughly a 40%/60% Non-RP to RP+ERP data ratio.
systems.adoption: 47.3K downloads, 93 likes on Hugging Face (verified via HF API).
systems.verification_note: License, training-data list, the Undi95 Unholy/LewdPlay lineage, the stated 40/60 data ratio, and download/like counts all confirmed directly from the model's own README and HF API metadata. The exact Llama 3 8B variant (base vs. instruct) used as the starting checkpoint is not explicitly named in the card.

systems.name: Cydonia 24B v4.3
systems.licence: Not declared in repo (base Mistral-Small-3.2-24B-Instruct-2506 is Apache-2.0, confirmed; an earlier Cydonia release, v2.1, carries a bare license:other tag with no accompanying text)
systems.price_note: Free to self-host; commercial terms not clearly stated by the fine-tuner
systems.context_window: 128k tokens (Mistral Small 3.2 architecture, confirmed); community feedback in the model's discussions reports strong coherence out to roughly 20k-32k tokens in practice
systems.best_for: Long-session, multi-character group roleplay with strong persona consistency and self-directed plot development — currently one of the most actively iterated mid-size community RP fine-tunes.
systems.watch: The v4.3 model card carries no license field at all, and the v2.1 release of the same series is tagged license:other with no explanatory text — treat commercial use as unresolved rather than assuming the Apache-2.0 base licence carries through unmodified.
systems.standout: Rapid-iteration series (v2 through v4.3 in under a year) built directly on user feedback threads about multi-character group-chat consistency and plot initiative, with an active 9,000+ member Discord (stated on the model card).
systems.architecture: Mistral Small 3 (dense, 24B)
systems.quantization_note: GGUF (including recommended iMatrix builds from bartowski) and EXL3 quantizations available.
systems.fine_tuning: Creative/roleplay-focused fine-tune of Mistral Small 3.2 24B Instruct; the author states the tuning explicitly deprioritizes benchmark intelligence in favor of writing quality, dynamism and reduced refusal behavior.
systems.adoption: 27.6K downloads, 142 likes on Hugging Face for v4.3 alone (verified via HF API); the wider Cydonia series (prior versions plus GGUF/EXL3 requants) has substantially more cumulative downloads.
systems.verification_note: Base model, parameter count, Discord size, and download/like counts confirmed via the model's own README and HF API metadata. Licence terms could not be confirmed — no license field is present in the v4.3 repo tags, and the prior v2.1 repo was independently confirmed to carry an undocumented license:other tag.

systems.name: MN-12B Mag Mell R1
systems.licence: Not declared in repo (a mergekit DARE-TIES combination of six Mistral-Nemo-based models, most individually Apache-2.0)
systems.price_note: Free to self-host; merge repo re-declares no licence of its own
systems.params: 12B parameters (Mistral Nemo architecture, dense mergekit DARE-TIES merge of 6 models)
systems.context_window: 128k tokens (Mistral Nemo architecture); the author tested sampler stability up to roughly 10k tokens
systems.best_for: Worldbuilding-heavy fantasy/adventure fiction and character roleplay — a widely used community merge praised for low "GPT-slop" prose and vivid, unexpected metaphors.
systems.watch: No license field is declared on the merge repo itself; because it blends six separately-licensed component models, downstream commercial use should be checked against each of those upstream repos rather than assumed.
systems.standout: Multi-stage DARE-TIES merge of six specialist Nemo fine-tunes grouped into 'Hero' (RP/trope coverage), 'Monk' (intelligence/groundedness) and 'Deity' (prose/flair) domains, rather than a single-dataset fine-tune.
systems.architecture: Mistral Nemo (dense, 12B) — mergekit DARE-TIES merge
systems.quantization_note: Official GGUF (Q4_K_M/Q6_K/Q8) from the author plus extensive third-party GGUF and EXL2 requants (RichardErkhov, mradermacher, and others).
systems.fine_tuning: Not a from-scratch fine-tune: a layer-weighted SLERP + DARE-TIES merge of Chronos-Gold-12B, MN-12b-Sunrose, mistral-nemo-bophades-12B, mistral-nemo-wissenschaft-12B, mistral-nemo-gutenberg-12B-v4 and magnum-v2.5-12b-kto over a ChatML-formatted Mistral Nemo base.
systems.adoption: 231.5K downloads, 248 likes on Hugging Face (verified via HF API); the author's own one-year-anniversary post states roughly 100,000 downloads on the full-precision weights alone.
systems.verification_note: Merge composition confirmed via the repo's own base_model tags. Release date corrected from an earlier draft's 'January 2025': the HF API's createdAt field reads 2024-09-16, independently corroborated by the author's own anniversary post. No license field is declared in the repo, so licence status is inferred from its upstream components rather than directly confirmed.

systems.name: Wayfarer 2 12B
systems.best_for: Text-adventure and game-master style roleplay where failure and consequences actually matter — trained specifically to let any character (including the player) die instead of defaulting to plot armor and positivity bias.
systems.watch: Trained exclusively on second-person present-tense narration ("you"); other perspectives work but the author notes results may be suboptimal.
systems.standout: Built by Latitude (the studio behind AI Dungeon) from simulated playthroughs where one LLM narrated and a separate, 'blind' LLM played the user — deliberately countering the positivity bias common in RP models, and playable live in AI Dungeon's own product.
systems.architecture: Mistral Nemo (dense, 12B)
systems.quantization_note: Official GGUF quantizations published alongside the full-precision weights.
systems.fine_tuning: SFT on the Wayfarer 2 text-adventure dataset (simulated AI Dungeon playthroughs) plus sentiment-balanced roleplay transcripts and a small instruct core, built in collaboration with Gryphe Padar (creator of the Pantheon-RP series).
systems.adoption: 19.7K downloads, 66 likes on Hugging Face (verified via HF API); also powers a free-play mode on Latitude's own AI Dungeon (aidungeon.com).
systems.verification_note: License, base model, AI Dungeon connection, Gryphe Padar credit, and second-person-only training all confirmed directly from the model's own README.

systems.name: Mistral-Nemo-12B ArliAI RPMax v1.1
systems.context_window: 8,192 tokens (the model's own stated training sequence length, per its README; the Mistral Nemo architecture it is built on separately supports up to 128k)
systems.best_for: Roleplay that avoids re-using the same phrases, personalities and situations across unrelated characters — a fully open-licence 12B tuned specifically to reduce cross-context formulaic 'slop' rather than adding more roleplay data volume.
systems.standout: RPMax's training recipe deliberately runs a single epoch over a heavily deduplicated dataset so the model, in the author's words, 'never sees a similar example twice' — a distinct methodology bet versus most RP tunes' multi-epoch approach.
systems.architecture: Mistral Nemo (dense, 12B)
systems.quantization_note: Extensively re-quantized to GGUF and EXL2 by third parties (QuantFactory, mradermacher, and others).
systems.fine_tuning: Full fine-tune using ArliAI's 'RPMax' recipe: deduplicated creative-writing and roleplay data, single epoch, lower gradient accumulation and higher learning rate than typical RP fine-tunes.
systems.adoption: 6.1K downloads, 47 likes on Hugging Face for v1.1 (verified via HF API); the RPMax recipe has since been extended by ArliAI to other base sizes at the same v1.1 versioning (Llama-3.1-70B, Mistral-Small-22B), though no v2 of the 12B line has shipped as of this research.
systems.verification_note: License, dedup-training methodology, download/like counts, and the RPMax extension to other base sizes all confirmed via HF API metadata and the model's own README. Two fields corrected from an earlier draft: the README's own text states 'Sequence Length: 8192', and states the base checkpoint is explicitly 'Mistral Nemo 12B Instruct 2407'.

systems.name: Magnum v4 72B
systems.price_note: Free to self-host, Apache-2.0; needs multi-GPU or heavy quantization at this size
systems.context_window: 32k tokens (trained/packed sequence length per the model's own training config; the Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct base itself supports up to 131k)
systems.best_for: Large-scale creative prose and character roleplay aimed at replicating Claude 3 Sonnet/Opus's writing register — the flagship of the well-known Magnum series for groups with the hardware to run a 72B model.
systems.watch: Dense 72B model needs substantial VRAM even quantized; the Magnum lineage has continued since via 'Magnum-Diamond' releases from Anthracite collective members (Doctor-Shotgun) on newer bases including Llama 3.3 70B and Mistral Small 3.2 24B, so this specific v4-72b checkpoint is no longer the newest generation.
systems.standout: Trained specifically on Claude-3 Opus/Sonnet-style instruct and writing logs (not generic instruction data) to replicate that prose register on open weights.
systems.architecture: Qwen2.5 (dense, 72B)
systems.quantization_note: GGUF quantizations published under anthracite-org and widely re-quantized by third parties.
systems.fine_tuning: Full-parameter fine-tune (8x MI300X GPUs, provided by DoctorShotgun) on Anthracite's Claude-3-Opus-derived writing/instruct logs and c2 roleplay logs, using a ChatML template with an explicit anti-purple-prose, anti-positivity-bias system prompt guideline.
systems.adoption: 47.7K downloads, 59 likes on Hugging Face (verified via HF API).
systems.verification_note: Base model, training hardware, sequence length (32,768), and the Magnum-Diamond follow-on releases (Doctor-Shotgun/L3.3-70B-Magnum-Diamond, Doctor-Shotgun/MS3.2-24B-Magnum-Diamond) all confirmed directly from the model's own README and independent HF repo searches. CONSOLIDATION PASS: changed the lifecycle facet from 'frozen' to 'superseded' — the row's own watch text states the lineage has moved on to Magnum-Diamond releases on newer bases, which is a superseded relationship, not merely a frozen/unmaintained one, so the facet was corrected to match the row's own prose.

systems.name: Pantheon-RP 1.6.1 12B Nemo

systems.best_for: Roleplay that needs a library of ready-made, switchable character personas — a two-thirds/one-third blend of persona-specific and general roleplay data so summoning a Pantheon character doesn't degrade non-Pantheon roleplay.

systems.name: Sweet Dreams 12B

systems.adoption: 1.9K downloads, 20 likes on Hugging Face as of this research (verified via HF API); a recent release relative to the rest of this list.
systems.verification_note: License, base model, dataset, release month, uncensoring rating, and format-flexibility claim all confirmed directly from the model's own README.

systems.name: DeepSeek-V4-Flash
systems.price_note: Free — self-host (open weights); MIT permits unrestricted commercial use
systems.context_window: 1M tokens (native; 384k+ recommended for the Think Max reasoning mode)
systems.best_for: Long-context agentic/reasoning work (up to 1M tokens) at a fraction of DeepSeek's own 1.6T V4-Pro flagship's compute cost, for teams that can dedicate a large multi-GPU or unified-memory box to it.
systems.watch: Ships in native FP4 (experts) + FP8 mixed precision rather than a standard checkpoint, so it doesn't drop into the llama.cpp/GGUF ecosystem as cleanly as DeepSeek-R1 did at launch — community GGUF requantizations exist but are newer and less battle-tested. systems.name: Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct
systems.best_for: A general-purpose local vision-language assistant for document OCR, screenshot/GUI understanding, and spatial grounding, backed by an unusually long native context window for a vision model.
systems.watch: The agentic GUI-action and 3D-grounding features are strongest in the larger 32B/235B siblings; the 8B dense variant trades some of that agentic accuracy for a footprint that fits on consumer hardware.
systems.standout: 256K native context (expandable to 1M) plus built-in agentic GUI/screenshot grounding — most local 8B-class VLMs top out well below this context length.
systems.architecture: Dense transformer VLM — ViT vision encoder + Qwen3 dense LLM
systems.quantization_note: Official GGUF quants (Qwen/Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct-GGUF): Q4_K_M ~5.0GB, Q8_0 ~8.7GB, F16 ~16.4GB; separate official FP8 checkpoint (~10.6GB) also published, though it targets H100/A100-class hardware via vLLM/SGLang rather than local llama.cpp use.
systems.fine_tuning: Community fine-tuning support via Unsloth and LLaMA-Factory guides (not an official Qwen release).
systems.verification_note: License, dense architecture, param count, and 256K/1M context confirmed directly against the Qwen/Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct model card. GGUF sizes corrected against the actual repo. Official FP8 checkpoint confirmed. Hardware tier is an estimate from the Q4_K_M file size, not a vendor-stated VRAM figure.

systems.name: Llama 3.2 11B Vision Instruct
systems.price_note: Free — open weights, self-host; custom Llama license, not OSI-approved
systems.best_for: A well-supported local VLM for image captioning, visual Q&A, and chart/document understanding, with near-day-one integration across vLLM, TGI, Ollama, and Transformers.
systems.standout: Broad ecosystem support among open VLMs — near-day-one integration into vLLM, TGI, and transformers, plus Ollama via its own runtime. This is NOT via mainline llama.cpp: ggml-org closed the mllama architecture-support request as 'not planned,' so community GGUF re-uploads exist but will not load in llama-server.
systems.architecture: Frozen Llama 3.1 8B text decoder + trained vision adapter (cross-attention layers feed image-encoder representations into the LLM)
systems.quantization_note: Unofficial int4/AWQ/GGUF community quants (e.g. unsloth bnb-4bit) bring VRAM to roughly 10-12GB; official BF16 weights need on the order of 24GB+. Community GGUF re-uploads exist (e.g. leafspark, pbatra) but do not load in mainline llama.cpp — ggml-org closed the mllama architecture-support request as 'not planned' (GitHub issue #9643); only Ollama's own patched runtime supports this model's cross-attention architecture.
systems.verification_note: License name, MAU-threshold clause, param count, context window, and benchmark figures confirmed directly against the meta-llama/Llama-3.2-11B-Vision-Instruct model card. CORRECTED: the draft's claim of full 'llama.cpp' support was false — ggml-org/llama.cpp closed the mllama architecture-support request as 'not planned' (issue #9643), so mainline llama.cpp/llama-server cannot load this model; only Ollama's own patched runtime does.

systems.name: InternVL3.5-8B
systems.best_for: Strong OCR, document, and chart understanding plus emerging GUI-agent and embodied-task grounding, from a lab that ships the same recipe across a full 1B-241B size range.
systems.standout: Ships in nine sizes from 1B to 241B (dense and MoE) under one evaluated architecture family, so the same training recipe scales down to edge or up to frontier-class hardware.
systems.architecture: Dense ViT-MLP-LLM (InternViT vision encoder + pixel-shuffle projector + LLM), trained with a two-stage Cascade Reinforcement Learning post-training recipe
systems.quantization_note: Community GGUF quants (bartowski, QuantStack) available: roughly Q4_K_M ~4.7GB up to F16 ~15-16GB; not an official OpenGVLab release. llama.cpp supports the InternVL architecture natively via its mmproj multimodal path.
systems.verification_note: License, param breakdown, 32K context window, and Cascade-RL/architecture description confirmed directly against the OpenGVLab/InternVL3_5-8B-HF model card. GGUF quant sizes are sourced from third-party community quant repos, so hardware tier is an estimate. CORRECTED: the draft's 'eleven sizes' claim was wrong — the family ships exactly nine sizes.

systems.name: MiniCPM-V 4.5
systems.best_for: Phone- and laptop-friendly image and video understanding — aggressive video-token compression makes it one of the few open VLMs that handles high-FPS, long-form video without a datacenter GPU.
systems.watch: The official PyTorch demo/video-benchmark path calls for a ~28GB GPU; realistic self-hosting depends on the published int4 or GGUF quantized weights instead of the BF16 checkpoint.
systems.standout: 96x video-token compression (6 frames -> 64 tokens) lets it complete a full Video-MME evaluation in ~0.26 hours versus roughly 3 hours for comparable open models, per the vendor's own reported figures.
systems.architecture: SigLIP2-400M vision encoder + Qwen3-8B LLM, with a unified 3D-Resampler that compresses up to 6 video frames into 64 tokens (96x compression)
systems.quantization_note: Official int4 build published (openbmb/MiniCPM-V-4_5-int4) alongside community GGUF and AWQ quants; unquantized BF16 weights alone are ~18GB.
systems.fine_tuning: Officially supported by LLaMA-Factory for fine-tuning as of September 2025 (merged via hiyouga/LlamaFactory PR #9022), per the project's own GitHub README.
systems.verification_note: License, param composition, max_position_embeddings (40960, read from config.json), and video-compression architecture confirmed directly against the openbmb/MiniCPM-V-4_5 model card and config. The Video-MME efficiency comparison was verified against the project's own docs table on GitHub. LLaMA-Factory support confirmed via the merged PR.

systems.name: Molmo2-8B
systems.price_note: Free — open weights, self-host; but see licence watch, effectively non-commercial
systems.best_for: Research and non-commercial local deployments needing pixel-level pointing/grounding and object tracking across video and multi-image sets, not just image description.
systems.watch: Despite the Apache-2.0 license on the weights, Ai2's own model card states the model 'is intended for research and educational use' and was trained on datasets 'subject to academic and non-commercial research use only.' Treat this as non-commercial until Ai2 publishes clearer commercial-use guidance.
systems.standout: Explicit pixel-coordinate pointing/grounding output plus frame-by-frame object tracking across video — most open VLMs only describe images, they don't point at or track objects within them.
systems.architecture: SigLIP2 vision encoder + Qwen3-8B LLM, with dedicated pointing/grounding output and frame-to-frame object-tracking capability
systems.fine_tuning: Full training code and nine training datasets released on GitHub (allenai/molmo2), though the datasets themselves carry non-commercial research-use terms.
systems.verification_note: License label, base composition, and max_position_embeddings (36864, read from config.json) confirmed directly against the allenai/Molmo2-8B model card and config. That same card states the model 'is intended for research and educational use', which is why licence_class is set to 'bad' despite the Apache-2.0 label on the weights themselves. Release date confirmed via Ai2's own press release. No official or community GGUF/quantized build was found, so the gpu-24 hardware tier is estimated from the ~18GB BF16 weight size.

systems.name: Pixtral 12B
systems.best_for: Multi-image document and chart reasoning from a model that was trained multimodal from scratch rather than adapter-tuned onto a frozen text model, able to process any number of images within its 128K-token context window.
systems.watch: Weights have not been updated since the September 2024 release — Mistral's newer multimodal work (Pixtral Large, Mistral Small 3.1) has since moved on at other size points, though the 12B checkpoint remains fully usable as-is.
systems.standout: Trained multimodal from the ground up rather than adapter-tuned onto a frozen text model, which shows in strong DocVQA (90.7 ANLS) and ChartQA (81.8) scores at a comparatively modest 12B size.
systems.architecture: Natively multimodal transformer — a 400M vision encoder trained jointly with the 12B decoder on interleaved image-and-text data from the start (no adapter-only fine-tune)
systems.quantization_note: Community GGUF quantizations with vision-projector (mmproj) files exist (bartowski, ggml-org) for llama.cpp/Ollama use, and llama.cpp's own multimodal docs list Pixtral as a supported vision architecture; exact file sizes were not confirmed against a primary Mistral source.
systems.verification_note: License, param count, 128k context window, and benchmark figures confirmed directly against the mistralai/Pixtral-12B-2409 model card and Mistral's own announcement page. GGUF quant availability and llama.cpp vision (mmproj) support confirmed via ggml-org's own multimodal docs, though exact file sizes not confirmed against a primary Mistral source. CORRECTED: the draft's specific 'up to roughly 2,000 images' figure could not be found in Mistral's official docs.

systems.name: Qwen3-0.6B
systems.best_for: A CPU-friendly default for on-device assistants and agent scaffolding that need a switchable thinking/non-thinking mode without a GPU.
systems.watch: Non-thinking-mode replies are noticeably terser than the thinking-mode traces most published benchmarks lean on — evaluate both modes separately rather than assuming one score covers both.
systems.standout: Shares the same chat template and Hermes-style tool-call format as the rest of the Qwen3 line, so an agent workflow built against the 32B model drops onto this 0.6B tier unchanged.
systems.architecture: Dense transformer, 28 layers, GQA (16 query / 8 KV heads)
systems.quantization_note: GGUF, AWQ and other community quantizations are widely available; the official card lists llama.cpp, Ollama, LM Studio, MLX-LM and KTransformers support directly.
systems.adoption: 184M+ cumulative Hugging Face downloads as of Aug 2026 research (matches Hub API download counter exactly).
systems.verification_note: License, parameter count, layer count, GQA head split and context window confirmed directly against the raw Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B README and Hugging Face Hub API metadata.

systems.name: Llama 3.2 1B
systems.price_note: Free — self-host only, gated download under Meta's Llama 3.2 Community License
systems.best_for: On-device summarization, rewriting and assistant tasks on phones — this is the size Meta paired with Qualcomm, MediaTek and Arm for shipping partners.
systems.watch: The Llama 3.2 Community License caps free commercial use at 700M monthly active users and requires 'Built with Llama' attribution.
systems.standout: Meta shipped official SpinQuant and QLoRA quantized checkpoints for this size; Meta's launch blog and the PyTorch/Arm ExecuTorch blog both report roughly 2.5x faster decode and about 56% smaller model size versus BF16, measured on-device via ExecuTorch on Android — though those figures are stated as averages across the 1B and 3B sizes together, not 1B-specific.
systems.architecture: Dense auto-regressive transformer with grouped-query attention (GQA)
systems.quantization_note: Meta ships official SpinQuant and QLoRA quantized checkpoints alongside the BF16 release; community GGUF conversions are also widely available.
systems.adoption: 57.5M+ cumulative Hugging Face downloads as of Aug 2026 research.
systems.verification_note: License, parameter count (1.23B, matching the card's own table), context window and gated status confirmed against the official meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B model card and Hub metadata. The on-device benchmark figures re-verified against Meta's official announcement blog and the PyTorch/Arm ExecuTorch blog directly.

systems.name: Gemma 3 270M
systems.price_note: Free — self-host only, gated download under Google's Gemma license
systems.best_for: A fine-tuning base rather than an out-of-the-box chat model — Google positions it for task-specific distillation and prototyping where even a 1-4B model is overkill.
systems.watch: Text-only despite the shared 'Gemma 3 is multimodal' framing on the family README — image input is a 4B/12B/27B-only capability. It is also trained on multilingual web text, but Google's own multilingual benchmark table only reports scores for the 1B/4B/12B/27B sizes, not 270M — treat multilingual quality here as unverified rather than assumed.
systems.standout: Ships with official QAT-trained quantized checkpoints on release day — confirmed native support in Ollama, llama.cpp and LM Studio for Q4_0 GGUF — and is explicitly positioned as the smallest Gemma 3 size, purpose-built for on-device fine-tuning rather than general chat.
systems.architecture: Dense transformer (gemma3_text)
systems.quantization_note: Official QAT checkpoints plus community GGUF quantizations (unsloth, bartowski, ggml-org, gaianet and others) are available; compatible with llama.cpp, Ollama and LM Studio.
systems.released: August 2025 (Gemma 3 family launched March 2025; 270M added afterward)
systems.adoption: 15.9M+ cumulative Hugging Face downloads as of Aug 2026 research.
systems.verification_note: Confirmed directly against the raw google/gemma-3-270m README, including the Inputs/Outputs section and the per-size multilingual-benchmark section.

systems.name: Gemma 4 E2B
systems.price_note: Free — self-host only, ungated download, Apache-2.0 weights
systems.best_for: The current on-device pick when you need multimodal (text, image, audio) understanding at phone-to-laptop scale under a genuinely permissive license.
systems.watch: The 5.1B total parameter count is more than double the '2.3B effective' figure Google markets — Per-Layer Embeddings make the on-accelerator compute footprint smaller than the checkpoint, so budget storage for the full 5.1B even though inference cost tracks closer to 2.3B.
systems.standout: Google moved Gemma 4 to a plain Apache-2.0 license with no gated download, dropping the custom Gemma Terms of Use that governed Gemma 1-3 — the biggest licensing change in the family's history, alongside native function-calling and a built-in thinking mode at this size.
systems.architecture: Dense transformer with hybrid local/global sliding-window attention and Per-Layer Embeddings (PLE)
systems.quantization_note: Official QAT-trained GGUF checkpoints plus community conversions are available; confirmed day-one support in llama.cpp, Ollama and LM Studio.
systems.adoption: 13.9M+ cumulative Hugging Face downloads as of Aug 2026 research, roughly four months after its April 2, 2026 launch.
systems.verification_note: License, parameter table, context window, hybrid attention + PLE architecture, and the multimodal/audio-support scoping confirmed directly against the complete raw google/gemma-4-E2B-it README. Release date corrected to April 2, 2026 (official launch blog), and gated-access claim corrected — the Hub API shows no gated-access flag on this repo.

systems.name: SmolLM3-3B
systems.price_note: Free — self-host only, Apache-2.0 weights and training recipe
systems.context_window: 64k tokens native, extends to 128k via YARN
systems.best_for: Teams that want the training data and recipe published alongside the weights — HuggingFace positions SmolLM3 as 'fully open,' not just open-weight, which matters for provenance audits.
systems.standout: Dual-mode reasoning (thinking/non-thinking toggle) plus two separate tool-calling interfaces (XML and Python-style) at 3B, reported at 92.3 on the BFCL agentic tool-use benchmark (no-extended-thinking mode).
systems.architecture: Dense decoder-only transformer, GQA + NoPE (3:1 ratio)
systems.quantization_note: GGUF, ONNX, MLX, MLC and ExecuTorch conversions are referenced directly on the model card for local and edge inference.
systems.adoption: 4.9M+ cumulative Hugging Face downloads as of Aug 2026 research.
systems.verification_note: License, parameter count, GQA+NoPE architecture, context window, dual-tool-calling interfaces and the BFCL 92.3 figure all confirmed directly against the raw HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM3-3B README and Hub API metadata (language tags: en, fr, es, it, pt, zh, ar, ru).

systems.name: MobileLLM-R1.5-950M
systems.price_note: Free for noncommercial research only — the license explicitly prohibits production/commercial use
systems.context_window: 32k tokens post-trained (4k for the base/pretrain checkpoint)
systems.best_for: Research and prototyping of math, code and science reasoning on sub-1B edge hardware where a commercial license isn't required — not a general-purpose chat model.
systems.watch: FAIR Noncommercial Research License v1 blocks production and commercial use outright — this is a research license, not a permissive one with a catch, so plan on a license swap or a different model before shipping anything.
systems.standout: Pretrained on roughly 2T tokens yet reported to beat DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B on math and coding benchmarks despite having about 60% as many parameters — data-efficient training, not scale, is the pitch.
systems.architecture: Dense transformer, 22 layers, 24 attention heads / 6 KV heads, 128k vocabulary, shared embeddings
systems.verification_note: License, parameter count, architecture and release date confirmed via the rendered facebook/MobileLLM-R1.5-950M model card and Hugging Face Hub API metadata. Supersedes facebook/MobileLLM-R1-950M via on-policy knowledge distillation per Meta's own release notes. No confirmed community GGUF quantization was found for the R1.5 checkpoint, so quantization_note and gguf-available facet were left off.

corrections.claim: The Llama 4 license carries forward Llama 3's anti-distillation clause, i.e. that outputs from Llama 4 models cannot legally be used to train competing LLMs.
corrections.reality: Meta removed the anti-distillation clause in the Llama 4 Community License (developer.meta.com/ai/llama4/license/, confirmed by direct fetch). The current text permits using Llama 4 outputs to train or improve other models, only requiring any resulting model be named with a 'Llama' prefix. The Llama 3 restriction does not carry forward to Llama 4.

corrections.claim: DeepSeek's models are MIT licensed across the board, since DeepSeek's GitHub repos say MIT.
corrections.reality: MIT applies to DeepSeek's code repositories, not necessarily to every model's weights. DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Lite-Instruct, for example, ships under a custom 'deepseek-license' HF tag (use-based restrictions including a no-military-use clause), confirmed by direct repo-file inspection — distinct from the MIT-licensed DeepSeek-V3.2/GLM-4.6-style releases also in this survey. Check the specific model's own license tag rather than assuming MIT from the org's reputation.

corrections.claim: A model with downloadable open weights (as opposed to an API-only proprietary model) is automatically usable in a commercial product.
corrections.reality: Several rows in this survey (Command R+, Aya Expanse 32B, Codestral-22B-v0.1, Molmo2-8B, Stheno v3.2, Llama-3-Lumimaid) have fully downloadable, self-hostable weights but are licensed CC-BY-NC, MNPL, or research-only terms that explicitly forbid commercial/production use. 'Open weight' and 'commercially usable' are independent axes, and this survey's licence_class field (open/warn/bad) exists specifically to separate them.

gaps: Multilingual is the thinnest category at 5 rows (vs. 6-10 elsewhere) — it clears the 3-row minimum but a buyer wanting broader regional coverage (e.g. dedicated African-language or Arabic-first models) will find less depth here than in general-chat or roleplay-creative. No suitable candidate for those specific gaps could be verified well enough to add without risking fabricated specs, so none was force-added.

No row in the entire 51-row set carries a populated `rating` field. Unlike this survey's TTS/Voices sibling section (which ships LMArena-style ratings on 27/168 rows), zero LLM rows here have a verified rating_source + rating_as_of pair. This is a genuine coverage gap, not an oversight — several candidate LMArena/Chatbot Arena Elo figures were considered during consolidation but none could be traced to a source specific enough (exact checkpoint, exact date) to attribute confidently, so all were left blank rather than guessed.

StarCoder2-15B and Codestral-22B-v0.1 both had their 'gguf-available' facet dropped during this pass because their quantization_note fields are null and no other field in either row evidences a GGUF build — GGUF quantizations for both models likely exist in the wild (they are popular enough), but this consolidation pass could not independently re-verify a specific GGUF repo for either within scope, so the facet was removed rather than left unsupported by the row's own text.

Hardware/VRAM figures for several of the largest MoE reasoning and general-chat rows (DeepSeek-V4-Flash, Kimi K2 Thinking, Qwen3-235B-A22B-Thinking-2507, Llama-3.3-Nemotron-Super-49B-v1.5) remain community estimates rather than vendor-published minimums, as already flagged by their own verification_note fields (marked 'mixed'). This is a real precision gap for buyers sizing hardware purchases against this survey.

The roleplay-creative category leans heavily on the Mistral-Nemo-12B lineage (5 of 9 rows — MN-12B Mag Mell R1, Wayfarer 2 12B, RPMax v1.1, Pantheon-RP 1.6.1, Sweet Dreams 12B — are all Nemo-12B-based fine-tunes/merges). This reflects genuine community concentration around that base rather than a curation error, but it does mean the category under-represents other base families (e.g. no Qwen- or Llama-3-based roleplay tune above 8B beyond the two frozen 2024 rows).

A cross-category duplicate-checkpoint check found one legitimate near-duplicate worth flagging explicitly (not dropping, per the task's own instructions): Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507 (general-chat) and Qwen3-235B-A22B-Thinking-2507 (reasoning) share the same 235B-A22B base model and MoE architecture but are genuinely distinct released checkpoints (non-thinking instruct vs. thinking-only) serving different purposes — kept as two rows, with a cross-reference note added to both.

Devstral-Small-2507 and Gemma-SEA-LION-v4-27B-IT are both marked status=dormant/facet=superseded because confirmed successors now exist (Devstral Small 2, SEA-LION v4.5). Neither successor was added as its own row in this pass since that would exceed the scope of a consolidation-only task — flagging this as a candidate for the next research round rather than silently leaving stale-looking 'active' rows in place.
